title: Match workloads to compute and pricing
prompt: A cost review of Lantern lists six proposals. Select every proposal that is a **sensible** match between the workload's shape and the compute or purchasing option.
hints: Ask three questions per proposal: how long does it run, how steady is it, and what happens if it is interrupted?
Spot is cheap because it can disappear with two minutes' notice. Which workloads tolerate that?
A Lambda invocation has a hard 15-minute limit.
explanation: Spot suits the archive job because it restarts safely, and the discount is large. A Savings Plan suits the baseline that runs every hour of the year, because a commitment is only good value when it is fully used. On-Demand is right for a three-week trial: no commitment for something that may not last. A 40-minute job cannot run in one Lambda invocation. A primary database on Spot would go down whenever AWS reclaims the capacity. And an always-on instance for an API that is idle most of the time pays for idle hours that Lambda would not charge for.

spot-batch.text: Run the nightly 40-minute poster archive, which can restart from a checkpoint, on Spot Instances.
spot-batch.why: Sensible. Interruptible batch work is exactly what Spot is for, and a restart costs only a few minutes.

sp-steady.text: Cover the always-on migration server, which will run all year at steady load, with a one-year Compute Savings Plan.
sp-steady.why: Sensible. Steady, predictable use is where a commitment pays off, because every committed hour is used.

lambda-long.text: Move the 40-minute archive job into a single Lambda invocation to stop paying for a server.
lambda-long.why: Not sensible. One Lambda invocation can run for at most 15 minutes, so the job would time out every night.

ondemand-trial.text: Run a three-week trial of a new search feature on On-Demand instances.
ondemand-trial.why: Sensible. Short and uncertain usage should not carry a one- or three-year commitment.

spot-db.text: Host the primary PostgreSQL database on a Spot Instance to save money.
spot-db.why: Not sensible. A database must not disappear on two minutes' notice; reclaimed capacity means an outage and possibly lost writes.

ec2-idle-api.text: Run the RSVP API, idle most nights and busy during big events, on a large always-on instance.
ec2-idle-api.why: Not sensible. You pay for idle hours and still risk running out of capacity in a spike. Lambda scales with requests and charges nothing when idle.
